observations.summary: Added optional query logging to ConnectionPool for production debugging
observations.detail: New queryLogger callback on PoolOptions logs SQL, params, duration (ms), and connection ID for every query() and execute() call. Disabled by default — zero overhead when not set. Enables N+1 detection and slow query tracing in production without code changes.

observations.summary: Added 9 new tests covering Repository CRUD, query logging, and pool edge cases
observations.detail: New tests: Repository.update (3: success, missing entity, maxSize=1), Repository.delete (1), Repository.count (1), query logging (4: query logging, prepared stmt logging, no-logger safety, param capture). All 119 total tests pass (70 auth + 49 repository).

observations.summary: Marked UserRepositoryAdapter as @deprecated with removal timeline
observations.detail: Added @deprecated JSDoc to UserRepositoryAdapter class and TODO comment with target removal in next major version. This makes the migration intent explicit in IDE tooling (strikethrough in VS Code) and searchable for cleanup.

observations.summary: Repository.update() acquires two pool connections sequentially — safe but suboptimal
observations.detail: update() calls this.findById() which acquires and releases a connection, then acquires a second connection for the UPDATE. Sequential acquisition avoids deadlock but doubles pool round-trips. Production optimization: combine into single UPDATE...RETURNING * statement. Confirmed safe at maxSize=1 via new test.

observations.summary: Updated review doc with round 2 findings, updated test counts
observations.detail: Added Follow-up Review section to docs/reviews/db-repository-pattern-review.md covering query logging, CRUD test coverage, adapter deprecation, and the update() double-acquire note. Updated test count table to 119 total.

observations.summary: UserRepository.findByEmail() should fall back to DB like findById() does
observations.detail: findById() checks in-memory cache then falls back to super.findById() via the pool. findByEmail() only checks the in-memory emailIndex and never queries the database. In a multi-instance deployment, a user created on another instance would be invisible. Consider adding a DB fallback query for cache misses.
